policy_title: Improve Crime Resolution, Justice for Victims, and Prison Reform
stated: Labour will reverse plummeting charge and prosecution rates by reducing barriers to bringing charges, cutting bureaucracy, and improving collaboration between police and prosecutors, including easier domestic abuse charging. They will boost investigation skills with a direct entry scheme for detectives. To address court backlogs, Associate Prosecutors will handle appropriate cases. Labour will increase the Victims’ Commissioner's powers, ensuring victims access information and support. They will review sentencing, build needed prisons, improve purposeful activity in prisons, support ex-offenders into work, identify and support children of imprisoned parents, and review probation governance, including devolved models.

source.quote: Labour will reverse this, driving up the proportion of crimes solved by reducing barriers to bringing charges, cutting bureaucracy, and improving collaboration. We will make it easier for highperforming police forces to charge domestic abuse suspects to speed up the process. Labour recognises recruitment challenges, particularly for detectives, so we will roll out a direct entry scheme for detectives to boost investigation skills. As an initial step to address the courts backlog, Labour will ensure more prosecutors are available by allowing Associate Prosecutors to work on appropriate cases. We will introduce new protections for victims of crime and persistent antisocial behaviour, by increasing the powers of the Victims’ Commissioner, and ensuring victims can access the information and support they need. Labour will carry out a review of sentencing to ensure it is brought up to date. Labour recognises that prisons are of national importance and therefore will use all relevant powers to build the prisons so badly needed. Labour will act to reduce reoffending. We will work with prisons to improve offenders’ access to purposeful activity, such as learning, and ensure they create pre-release plans for those leaving custody. The children of those who are imprisoned are at far greater risk of being drawn into crime than their peers. We will ensure that those young people are identified and offered support to break the cycle. Labour will conduct a strategic review of probation governance, including considering the benefits of devolved models.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets crime resolution rates, charge/prosecution barriers, court backlogs, victims' support, sentencing, prison capacity and probation — core indicators of whether safety and justice work.
The policy explicitly commits to supporting ex-offenders into work, a concrete employment intervention with a direct mechanism affecting employment rates and in-work poverty for that population.

Easier domestic abuse charging improves equal access to justice for a disproportionately affected group; expanded Victims' Commissioner powers strengthen due process and rule-of-law protections for victims.

Building new prisons is a major capital expenditure; expanding detective entry, associate prosecutors, and Victims' Commissioner capacity adds ongoing operational cost — the funded/borrowed balance is materially affected without a specified funding source.

membership_note: Four fundamentals: O5 is the primary target across the full justice chain; O9 is triggered by the domestic-abuse and victims'-due-process elements; O4 by the explicit ex-offender employment strand; O12 by the prison-building programme and staffing expansion whose funding is unspecified.
